name: Tom Perriello
subject: Final Vote Counted. History Lies Ahead.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TOM PERRIELLO FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | | |
---
| | |
---
Dear Friends, With the final votes counted and the race certified, we narrowed the margin to one point, moving the district 14 points from 2024 and nearly 7 points from Gov. Spanberger’s historic performance just last year. I just completed a thank you tour of the district, and dozens of people are already making plans to run for local and state office in 2027 – and our new Dem-majority City Council in Lynchburg is making plans to govern! The momentum you helped us create is still rippling across our region of Virginia. I wanted to take this moment to say thanks and to offer you a few thoughts on what this race has meant, beyond just the numbers. Here are my top ten takeaways from this campaign:
---
1. **Dems must show up everywhere and fight for every community.** We closed the margin by 14 points by making gains in every single one of the 21 counties and 3 municipalities. We visited every corner of this district, over and over again. From day one, we knew it was as important to make gains in our reddest counties as it was to maximize turnout in our bluest.
2. **Rural Virginia is not all red – and not all white.** One of my greatest hopes about Dem victories around the country is that the party will finally understand that rural regions include a lot of small towns that are getting bigger, bluer, and more diverse. We moved our rural counties 10 points bluer. We worked with farmers – white and Black – to release our FED UP agenda, and we enlisted over 200 doctors and nurses from across the district to endorse us and spread the word about the deep and growing cuts to rural health services caused by HR1. When you show up, listen, and actually fight for people they notice. My most urgent and public hope for our new Dem majorities in Congress is that they move immediately in January, not through regular order, to prevent the Medicaid and SNAP cuts that will further devastate rural communities. On Day One, they can bring down costs by removing authorization for this war and these tariffs, and on day two move swiftly to prevent a generational closure of health services across rural America.
3. **We turned Lynchburg blue and helped to elect the first Dem-majority City Council in a generation.** In the home of Liberty University, we worked seamlessly with three amazing local leaders to flip the city council, and that council appoints the School Board. Our race helped to bring resources and attention to areas that have seen little or no investment from the party. During my thank you tour around the district, I was moved to see how many people who worked with our campaign are now thinking about running for local or state office in 2027 to keep this momentum going!
4. **UVA students showed up in record numbers!** UVA students turned up to vote in even larger numbers than in the 2024 Presidential cycle. That is incredible! With a lot of leadership from campaign manager Lily Franklin – who had tripled student turnout at Virginia Tech in her race for Delegate the previous year – we exceeded all expectations for engaging young people in this campaign.
5. **We prioritized real grassroots operation.** 13,000 donors. More than 1,000 volunteers. 300,000 contact attempts. 50,000 doors knocked. 25,000 personal conversations. No corporate PAC money. No lobbyist money. Just y’all.
6. **Main Street populism builds our coalition, when we help communities stand up to corporate greed.** From fighting to block the Valley Link Transmission Line and data centers to fighting to protect rural health clinics, we made it a priority at every stage of the campaign to stand with communities fighting corporate greed and corruption. We ran 6 points ahead of the Democratic benchmark in this district and 14 points ahead of where we were in 2024. A campaign built on lower costs, common sense, and standing up to powerful interests can win rural Virginia.
7. **You believed in us, even when the national party did not.** This campaign ran on your donations. The national party chose not to make a real financial investment in our race, even when the polls showed it was winnable, but you believed in this race early and invested in us. McGuire had to get a late influx of millions to eke this out, and we did not get the same party support on our side, but you gave us the resources to fight this to the last vote.
8. **Be prepared everywhere, because you never know what the next election might look like.** Mississippi and Texas were ready, because state and regional leaders had been building for this kind of a year for many years. Two years ago, any rational pundit would have considered VA-05 unwinnable, but our campaign in this political environment proved otherwise. We cannot know what factors and demographics will shape the next few elections, so we need to keep fighting everywhere and for everyone. We need to be ready.
9. **The American people want national protections from AI, ASAP.** If we are looking for an issue that unites Americans on the right, left and center, it is the intense and broad demand for regulations, liability, and guardrails on AI. Perhaps my most pleasant and persistent surprise on the campaign trail was seeing the voters being so far ahead of both parties in their readiness for a national conversation, mobilization, and agenda around AI. I shared some of those thoughts in [The New Republic](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143420453/660152806/1269056589?refcode=261113em_tp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjIxMDkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDVmMDE5NTAtYmZkZi1mMTExLTkxZjAtMDAwZDNhMThlMjQ0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VLZjCnriz4ZdFdrY8gRUHCEmGgMLVK5QwL6607QbFQY=&emci=01c9cb79-bedf-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=45f01950-bfdf-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=18671963) [here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143420454/660152819/1269056589?refcode=261113em_tp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjIxMDkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDVmMDE5NTAtYmZkZi1mMTExLTkxZjAtMDAwZDNhMThlMjQ0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VLZjCnriz4ZdFdrY8gRUHCEmGgMLVK5QwL6607QbFQY=&emci=01c9cb79-bedf-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=45f01950-bfdf-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=18671963).
10. **America finally got the 250th Anniversary celebration we deserved!** In every generation since our founding, America has faced questions of who gets to count as fully American and fully human, of whether we will be a more perfect Union that lives up to our bold promises of inalienable rights and equality under the law. The current Administration used every second of every day to create a dark storm cloud over this 250th year that should have been a chance to celebrate the enduring American experiment. Last Tuesday, we, the people, gave ourselves the greatest possible anniversary gift – a resounding national chorus of America the Beautiful, sung through every vote cast from the Delta to Detroit and Austin to Alaska, and yes from Charlottesville to Chatham and Lynchburg to Louisa. So many of us stepped up to run this year – and to donate, to knock doors, to poll watch – because we knew the future of our country was on the line. Together, through our victories and even our noble defeats, we dared not just to prevent the end of American democracy but also to make it more resilient, inclusive, and expansive than it has ever yet been.

---
For that, I say thank you. For that, I say congratulations. For that, let us celebrate, rest, and prepare for the work that must continue ahead. With love and determination, Tom

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3994%2E259176%2Eb9zTDt) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3994%2E259176%2Eb9zTDt)_

If we haven’t met before, I’m a native of northwestern North Carolina who's spent forty years of my career working in local journalism, and I'm also the Democrat who is currently up by **335 votes** against Virginia Foxx, _**the second most-powerful Republican in the House.**_

This is the closest House race in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.

As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files. When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, _**all while making millions playing the stock market.**_

Meanwhile, I spent my career reporting the truth at the local newspaper my grandfather started after WWI. I always made an effort to bring my readers just the facts without any bias. In that same spirit, my team and I are working around the clock to make sure every legal ballot in this race counts, because no matter _who_ they voted for, _all_ of our neighbors deserve to be heard.

**For the first time in decades, North Carolina’s Fifth District will be represented by a Democrat.** I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work to lower costs and fight corruption in Washington – but Republicans are going to do all they can to ensure this doesn’t happen. **They’re going to challenge every single vote.** Just 335 votes could end Virginia Foxx’s political career and the decades of nastiness – **but this week will be the most critical of the campaign.** I need your help now to ensure we have the resources required to defend this seat and make sure our neighbors are heard. subject: Tell Your Senator: It's Time for New Leadership!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe
body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

The calls to replace Chuck Schumer are growing louder — and Our Revolution
is officially backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1011&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]Photo of Chris Van Hollen

After a historic election that put Democrats back in control of Congress,
the message from the grassroots couldn’t be clearer: It’s time for new
leadership and a Democratic Party that’s ready to FIGHT.

In our post-election survey of 4,308 Our Revolution supporters, 72% said
Chuck Schumer is NOT the right person to lead Senate Democrats.

Now, senators are beginning to make their decisions about who they’ll
support for leader — and we need to make sure they hear from US.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1012&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]ADD YOUR NAME: Tell your senators to support Chris Van Hollen for
Senate Majority Leader!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1013&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]SIGN THE PETITION →

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1014&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]Headline: Chris Van Hollen launches challenge against Chuck Schumer to
lead Senate Democrats

We're delivering your signatures to the Senate on Tuesday, November 17th.
This is our chance to send a powerful message before senators cast their
votes.

Our Revolution is proud to endorse Chris Van Hollen because he’s shown
he’s willing to challenge the party establishment, stand up to powerful
corporate interests, and fight for a Democratic Party that puts working
people first.

As Our Revolution Executive Director Joseph Geevarghese put it:

"Working people organized to win this majority, and they expect it to
fight for them."

We didn’t organize millions of voters, flip the House and Senate, and
elect a new generation of progressive fighters just to watch Democratic
leaders return to business as usual.

We need leaders who will take on Trump AND the billionaires and corporate
donors who have too much power over BOTH parties.

Leaders who will fight for Medicare for All, get corporate money out of
politics, and stand up for working families — even when it means
challenging their own party.

That’s the kind of leadership we’re fighting for. And that’s why we’re
backing Chris Van Hollen.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1015&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]TELL YOUR SENATORS — SUPPORT VAN HOLLEN!

For ten years, Our Revolution has fought to transform the Democratic Party
from the bottom up — helping elect more than 1,300 progressive champions,
mobilizing millions of voters, and challenging the corporate
establishment.

Now, with a new progressive wave heading to Washington, we have a chance
to change not just WHO holds power, but HOW that power is used.

But the decision is being made NOW. Senators are lining up behind their
preferred candidates, and we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1016&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]Add your name TODAY. We’ll deliver your signatures on Tuesday, November
17th, and demand that Senate Democrats choose Chris Van Hollen as their
next leader.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40124?source=email-20261113&t=1017&akid=11599%2E5885482%2EMCWUlW ]ADD YOUR NAME BEFORE NOV. 17 →

We fought to win this majority. Now we’re fighting to make it deliver.

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

| | First, thank you to our supporters and voters. This process only works when candidates earn the trust of the public, and we're incredibly grateful to everyone who put their faith in Jonny and this campaign.
I'm happy to report that I've already updated my FEC Form 2 to reflect my **2028 run for Congress!**
The nationwide blue wave didn't skip Utah. There were several Democratic wins in the 4th Congressional District, including **Jess Birtcher** , who defeated anti-union Jordan Teuscher, and fellow veterans **Shana Anderson** in Senate District 19 and **Drew Howells** in House District 39. Many other Democrats also came remarkably close to victory, performing much better than predicted.
The entire state moved to the left, and we're optimistic that this progress will continue. Take a look below at how Jonny's share of the vote compares with previous Democratic candidates in today's 4th Congressional District. FEDERAL JUDGE SETS HEARING ON UNSEALING ILHAN OMAR SEARCH WARRANT
RECORDS

A federal judge has ordered a November 17 hearing on our push to
unseal records from the FBI search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s
home—including the warrant, affidavits, and evidence supporting the
search.

Chief Judge James E. Boasberg set a hearing
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86580&L=39194&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL29tYXItc2VhbGVkLXNlYXJjaC13YXJyYW50LWhlYXJpbmctMDAxMTQtMDAxNDcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=01b93a117a75d1e750497544cb2c2a636fa24cd0e8b57adee8f7ea9f491a4f81]
for next week on our and media requests to unseal the search warrant
and other records on the October 12 search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s
(D-MN) home (_In re Application of Fourteen Press Organizations for
Access to Sealed Search Warrant Records_, No. 1:26-mc-00144 (D.D.C.)).

On November 12, 2026, Boasberg issued the following order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86580&L=39194&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL29tYXItc2VhbGVkLXNlYXJjaC13YXJyYW50LWhlYXJpbmctMDAxMTQtMDAxNDcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=01b93a117a75d1e750497544cb2c2a636fa24cd0e8b57adee8f7ea9f491a4f81],

We filed a motion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86580&L=38971&F=T&&H=a3a37918649d932e9c3643fb5ee92c7856047fdc4c745a850e0d00cf1e65bec0]

October 12 search of Omar’s home, including the warrant, its
application, supporting affidavits and attachments, any return and
inventory, the docket sheet, and related briefs, motions, orders,
opinions, and transcripts. The request includes records concerning the
scope of the search and the court's decision to seal the materials.

We noted its interest in allegations concerning Omar predates the
search. On July 23, 2019, we filed an ethics complaint
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86580&L=38931&F=T&&H=e49c43089e7f2ac885ddb55065ec0843405328eff6ce3a6987cb44992c0a508c]
to the Office of Congressional Ethics requesting an investigation into
allegations of perjury, immigration fraud, marriage fraud, state and
federal tax fraud, and federal student loan fraud.

We argue that the public has a right to access the warrant records
under both common law and the First Amendment. Its motion states:

> [T]he public’s need for access is substantial. The government has
> searched an elected official’s home and has publicly acknowledged
> an ongoing criminal investigation, even to the point of commenting
> on its conduct. Representative Omar has disputed the government’s
> account and used the search and those comments to solicit campaign
> contributions. News reports based on unnamed sources have added

Fellow Republicans of the 5th District,

The 5th District GOP Chair Convention is today, Saturday, November 14, at Fork Union Military Academy. If you are a Delegate, you should show up 9am.

Virginia and our country face serious challenges. We need serious leadership in the 5th, leadership focused on winning elections, not internal games and retribution.

Ramona's opponent is supported by the current leadership. I'm not going to attack Ramona's opponent. But I am disappointed in the name-calling and false attacks that have taken place. We as a party can do better. Our energy belongs on defeating Democrats, not tearing each other down.

For too long, the 5th has been distracted by division at the exact moments we needed unity. The fact that we were the only one of Virginia's eleven congressional districts forced into a convention during this critical midterm is just one more reason we need new leadership. Maybe a better focus would have saved Rob Wittman.

Ramona Christian is that leadership.

While helping me win a race where even Democrats told me just yesterday they threw everything they could at us and were surprised we won, Ramona was key to our win. She worked tirelessly building relationships in every corner of the 5th District. She knows our counties, our activists, and what it takes to organize and win. She is ready on day one to lead the 5th District Committee, grow our party, and help turn Virginia red again.

I am proud to support Ramona Christian for 5th District Chair, and I urge you to show up and do the same.

See you tomorrow at Fork Union.

👋 Good morning, Peter. Today is Saturday, November 14th, and VoteVets has an important message. 🇺🇸
The fight to stop Trump’s arch is escalating quickly, and we need your help to fight back while there’s still time.

Late last week, a federal commission stacked with Trump allies heard more than 9 hours of public testimony on his 250-foot Arc de Trump. The arch would leave a permanent stain on more than 50,000 graves at Arlington National Cemetery, and Veterans and military families voiced their concerns.
The commission approved it anyway.
But right before they broke ground, a federal judge _blocked_ construction for at least 5 more days.

**There’s a reason why Trump’s allies are trying to ram this through right after the election, Peter: They’re hoping you’re too distracted to notice. We cannot let them succeed.**
Every Veteran in America deserves to know what Trump wants to do to Arlington Cemetery. VoteVets is working to raise enough hell so they can’t force the Arc de Trump through in secret.

[**Please, chip in $5 or more to help VoteVets stop this draft dodger’s arch. Nothing would make Donald Trump angrier than a huge amount of people stepping up today.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261114-1-misc&t=1&akid=35798%2E3013755%2EWjucZE)

**It was also the most _expensive_ midterms in history**, after GOP megadonors poured more than a BILLION dollars into beating us. But these Democrats overcame that historic challenge to win their races and help deliver the Senate majority!

Now we're gaining new fighters against the GOP's harmful agenda ‐‐ and with an uncalled race in Alaska, one more could still be on the way! _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3999%2E259176%2E_GW-qS) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3999%2E259176%2E_GW-qS)_

I'll cut to the chase, Peter. [**I’m reaching out to ask: Will you split a $26 contribution between me and Blue Amp Action for our recount fund to confirm our victory in MN-01?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20141?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.14_Jjohnson-Recount-3_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=3999%2E259176%2E_GW-qS) We're up against a major challenge and I know time is tight, so I hope you'll give me a moment to explain why this matters right now. On Tuesday night, voters made their choice, and I won the race for MN-01 by over 300 votes.

Brad Finstad has called for a recount, and we’re confident that I will be confirmed as the new Congressman in southern Minnesota.

The problem we're facing is that we spent down to zero through Election Day to win, after Finstad won his last election by 17 points.

I hate to ask, but here’s why we need more funds. The recount itself will likely be funded by taxpayers, because Finstad has the ability to request that under state law. **However, that doesn’t cover all the staff and observers we need on our end to ensure that we can advocate for ourselves during the recount process across all 21 counties.** [With this serious challenge in front of us, I’m hoping you can chip in a contribution of $26 between me and Blue Amp Action today. subject: It’s like being the new kid at school
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1818?t=1001&akid=3906%2E251025%2EwxpUi9 ]Abdul El-Sayed Senator-elect for Michigan [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1818?t=1002&akid=3906%2E251025%2EwxpUi9 ]Abdul El-Sayed Senator-elect for
Michigan

Hey Peter,

I just got back from Washington, where I took part in orientation as your
senator-elect.

Walking in on the first day was surreal. Honestly, it felt a lot like
being the new kid at school.

I met up with many of my fellow freshmen, and chatted with a few folks who
currently serve.

Most people never hear about this. They don’t see what happens after
winning. Usually the emails stop, and the candidate disappears.

That’s not what I’m planning to do here. Instead, I’m taking you on this
journey with me,
Peter.

For months, we took on the power of corporations and billionaires and
special interests, and you held the line the whole way.

That tireless support paid off, and now, the real work (and fun!) begins.

I'll be sworn in on January 3, 2027. From now until then, our transition
efforts will be focused on building a team, getting ready to serve, and
setting things up so I can deliver for Michigan from day one.

Just like with our campaign, our transition work is fueled 100% by people
like you, not corporate PACs. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261114-1-ak.-nOuZ2&amount=10&refcode=em20261114-3901&t=1004&akid=3906%2E251025%2EwxpUi9 ]So if you’re able to pitch in a few bucks
to help me hit the ground running in the new year, I’d be so grateful:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261114-1-ak.-nOuZ2&amount=10&refcode=em20261114-3901&t=1023&akid=3906%2E251025%2EwxpUi9 ]Donate $10 ››

In solidarity,

Abdul

The bill carves out criticism of any Muslim-majority country comparable to criticism directed at other countries, and it includes a clause stating that nothing in the act shall be construed to diminish rights protected by the First Amendment or the New Jersey Constitution, or to conflict with existing anti-discrimination laws.

Public officials and law enforcement officers reviewing alleged violations of the state's civil and criminal anti-discrimination laws would be required to take the definition into account when deciding whether an act was motivated by Islamophobia and discriminatory anti-Muslim intent. ## Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Halts Flights
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights Friday, following a communication issue affecting air traffic control centers, [halting travel at airports across the country](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OrDAMBeCnCV1G-YVQpLgN3dx2SxQSA5YyAREPo337FewjbG3LPt_5eo7PgBnL8j-8wBPNY4FPzUAEx1gC4VY-mGAOYTm2d0mVtn2CUQnVcim5NGOIhCeMJjTJT0r2wcQGvOx601pjpWhW72SwWrgo2sn1Uds-dabt7WR1itFC26C_DkopjZTCKffQyanO2Sj11HWT0cwISEjb8aAVCEqBWgHm_L2dcDzi9mqyX4n2yvQ_pgamhrBfkGvE1JDxBKaGXwK_DDyceOv4nHFZqfJrnb_3FAjqTdP8CtUcPu0fzBlr2zEjllfAfH-kP9Z1evUTAAD__wLDfzE). As of 8:45 p.m. EST, the FAA said airplane departures could resume after the agency lifted the nationwide ground stop. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said FAA technicians were investigating. At [Nashville International Airport](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2unTAMwPGnCVsQccLHGTJ0YbtdOyJDzCFSSFDiS3TevqId-gBdvFj6y_79-lq-0Acf3z_xJMu8L5FqCcRMeYnIPsXqHe2I75y-oyucrpUW6GCQSkllFtzY37QYbJxdQb3QbA1ZNb7M0Jtedc1hte5fsLmdjIPBAbitc_1ACHroej1i4-0TVEoZpboJpla7Ccap35Rex3E1WpiOnOeUWz6IKUYqhWgPn3RTbrd0NsEezFcR-oeAWcBca21rOe9nKWB--gJmpZ6hBcwRy3H7EEiiz1fKLB1dmPk7k1wTZldkOVKVz_flyoROOgr4KRJ3piz_2ci_MvKhETA32bqr-hB8GUZhuveJPvw5kf_T97bwOwAA__8tkZGI), flight boards showed widespread delays and several cancellations, leaving travelers stranded and scrambling. Travelers should check with their airlines for the latest flight status. [Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGunDAQxvHTmM6IMWYNhYs0dJs2JRrweLFi7BWexcrtI5LiHeA1U_41v-_Xc3liiCG9fuJBltkviWqJxEznkpBDTjU48oivM3-SK5zfKy2qUw8JIEEvuHG4aNHYOLsqmFBvDVkwk34MeoCu2S06dGbSWrtp8g60d8Ng_OppHcA4MzbB3kEA0ADdqMa2d6My47BBvxqz6l7ojlzgfLa8E1NKVAqRj3_yRWe75aOJdmd-F9H_EGoWaq61tvWK3PIl1HznhZoB7qOFmj2iDKV8qMgvpfxvlDdSFtpycpLDQbKEtJGcAGTdkeXvlKtQc3Na964hxlAeRujudWCI_57hby55WfU3AAD___t8iGw) said there was no indication that a national security threat caused the outage, though he did not rule out any cause, including a cyberattack. The ground stop is only the second nationwide halt since the Sept. 11 attacks, following a 2023 outage.

## Ground Stop Strands NC Travelers
A rare nationwide ground stop halted every departure from North Carolina's airports for more than four hours Friday. ## Rivers Comes Home to NC State
NC State hired former Wolfpack quarterback Philip Rivers as its head football coach Friday. The 44-year-old [signed a five-year deal](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0LGOpDAQBNCvMZkR3dgYBw4uIZtLL0TGboaWDEbGGm7_fjWzn7BxSVV69e8xPzwnPp5__U5uPcJ80H0lqpXKXPhF5Qp5p2vLO9V8hKv6SnHGDgcJIEHNZ8nXSaHO0ERnTD_Y2JADY9Wgle5ss7lIo-ksLWgGC7j2y9KDH9EuajShW0PD7l0IAAqgG9G2YwzLilFZrbWl0QrVUeSaS7umr_yicuRSt-BLTnz4NuS9SW6r9bxE_0fgJHC677u9_zMDvmOBky-VQyKB07lx4lP-8OQR5EclN_JRrjnXxackQ_ZhEzgZpVBrDU1x8bw5Jb4GI1T33D2nz3L97W8vh98BAAD__83ng20) and will be introduced Monday. ## Cherokee County Residents Protest Data Center
Cherokee County residents protested outside their electric cooperative’s office Tuesday over a possible data center near Grape Creek Road. Neighbors [learned of the project](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMRp_G3hhYiuRYg4cu3m7XjgYj0ddC9GNIdFK_faECfYJuBL9zCJK_vtYv9MGn758Yad6SXRN9aiBmKmvxbyrV5kh1z5E4J1sZmdwqBzmCECDUepRcD7K8it7Nj8d9NK6nWTyMGrXSg-n3WbrNGKW1UpMli1ppjXi3k1GjU0bb3s9toBBCCTFM0twmZ5-bbKHWhibTqYGc51xuW7jym0rKhXeLJQef8GZz7MO8Mx-1u__o5NLJJeYzMfr0u6WdXNpdnVxsjvFMni_419ip5BcR2CZcUKh6R4krbPlMDvLJgA0Gh4xgKTGVBgcHTwKfgHeCTy6v2qoLsFBi2PE4LsBn0z13cunL7I6PD8HX8dGp4TuiD3835__9-3uWfwIAAP__atudTg) from Blue Ridge Mountain EMC workers placing survey flags near their land. ## Season's First Freeze Arrives
The [coldest air of the season](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAQhp9GMyxA1JmA4BKzufRCq4UGqUOwoHfc2affcmrfYJOOur76v-_fY3lAiCH5v7CjJu-WhGeNSIRlcaFUcgXxC7cPH_GV8h4SEC6Sy5EJwYRajpLrgYYW0Vrdc4tC3VrUYrqrcVBTr9pN2xXvBlY12vukOLjB8XXsV-76id_MyNugL6IQQgkhpFCdnLiTq8GBgwW89Y3iaAPl0tGGHnPxAVx85SeWzuS9jXojOmrT_2nk3Mj5PM_O5c8BKEIiuH4aOV9ujZyhGAqGrREqsbWE5EPyLOVCG_thV_aWZ67k970asBPxPybbFm2PM8QY6jg1ivsdQnyvoN8WfGr5HQAA___PDYpX) has settled over the state, with a freeze warning in effect until 9 a.m. today for much of north and west Georgia. Forecasters expected lows of 25 to 30 degrees across north Georgia overnight, with a hard freeze in the mountains and frost possible around metro Atlanta. Highs will stay in the 50s this weekend. The freeze threat spreads farther south Sunday morning. Southeast Georgia is under a [freeze watch](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQgOGnMR3IMziYFC6uocu1VyLHjMG3BiN7Eiv79Kus9g22_qWv-P_d5psNMRzrX7uT4dXPB9USiZny7EMu7DPRJ22PNdLrSHs4LNOMEocWoAU1nzmVkxzP0CymlwuBGhsyoK9quCjdq2YzvUbyHuButR60t875kQboEa6X0V5VE8xbBAAFAAiqQy093h1dpF0sjb1QkpbAKXe80Uopr8H6-EpPyp1LexPNxnwW0f8ROAmcaq1d_e_iOwqcbObgIgmcSnrwRrZw-6O0MVWXHgfnV-tzKtzyFkpbiT7oWAROWimUQy-bbJazhhhDGbRQct1t-PYb_u24p8GvAAAA__8JdIUE) late tonight into Sunday, with inland lows in the low to mid 30s and lower 40s at the coast. In South Georgia, [patchy frost is possible early Sunday](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGupDAQBNDTmMyINgaGwMEmZLPphshjt8Fag1G7d6zZ03_xr_CTSkp6KtWf5_q0McVz-20PNLyF9cRaEjIjrSFS4UCI_3H_tyX8nPmIp2VcVadGCSBBrxflcqHjFRpv-s4j6EeDBqZZj4Oeet3sZhpdGMHalx713M9qGILzbu7m3s0A49REc4sAoAFAgW7V1AX1cjh01lt89EJ36CNnannHDTNt0Yb0yW-k1uWjSWZnvorofwm1CLXUWttq0-suhVpuXagF4I5eqIXQ-o_MJM_MssaTkaQlim8sskbepcvJS8bjKjJQLix5j0VWxL94eqGWhoy_akwplnESutsOG9P3FP7pjW-jvgIAAP__mrCICA), and freezing temperatures are most likely north and west of Albany. Forecasters urge residents to protect people, pets, plants, and pipes.
## Hugley Nominated as House Speaker
Georgia House Democrats nominated Rep. Carolyn Hugley of Columbus for speaker Thursday, putting her in line to become the [first black speaker in state history](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAQhU-DM7cojP8Cgk2c9aYbWrVQGLTYWFDdrd7TjzwzN5jkRU_f-_lzX-8YUzy237iT4c2vB71qImYqq4-lsi9E_yk8tkTvI-_xQKZVSTW0AC3o9Sy5nmR5hcaZTjoCPTVkYJz10Oux000wUzfMs_fYWav7fkYvQY7g7WwnmLXum2guIgBoAFCgb2qUXv211Et0SFMntCQXOZcbB9ooly2iT-_8pHKzeW-SCcxnFd0voRahlpIfW3AFPSMnPBgvl1DLFSPUAnCJEmr5ZrUhPyq1jvZsC3Jtvwa39ST8R6VNhI5KDfEUammKcecrphTrMAottx1j-qzBP73wadRHAAAA__8I1Ic-). If the full House confirms her in January, Hugley would succeed Speaker Jon Burns, R-Newington, and become the first woman elected to a full term in the post. Republican Rep. Jan Jones served as acting speaker from late 2022 into 2023. Democrats also chose Rep. Billy Mitchell of Stone Mountain for speaker pro tem and Rep. Stacey Evans of Atlanta as majority leader. Hugley said [Medicaid expansion comes first](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OtCAUxZ8GOwz3ijpTUHyN3XztlgblomRBDOCY2affuH-eYJvTnOSXc35vj_GhnXfb8l8HUmWx40Zn9lQKpdG6lItNRB-0Houn1xaD23ShEQV2HICDHPcU805zGaEyqhGGQN4qUtDfZdfKvpHVqlrRSiO6Sd4RJoP9hFoLsMYaY-kOVDl1EQFAAgCCrLEXFqeZWqGNplvDpCDjSkx1WWmhmBanrX_FJ6V6jqHyai1lz6z5x3BgOJznWZ_lGa6S4XDRGQ4AVyDD4QfB13hk4oZCnJMumf8-5HP0R5iOzBPtfNYp-tfGvy3wvJN-p8RwqJIy--m8d7nrmRRL0M5_DSp_lflU-BkAAP__GhGLvA) but cautioned, _"I don't want to give anybody any false notions that things are going to change overnight."_ Republicans, who kept a slim state Senate majority, [have said they won't budge](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMGK6jAYRp8m3aU0f1NbF1lcvWQYQZkBQWdVYvOnDaZNSaLFefrBwTeY9QeH75zTvt0r6-zUH9SIIvWmnXCJDlPC0BobYjIB8RuHW-_wMfnRTiphCwWsKGOU8XYOPs7YpZZlWpSFRsabDAWr13xV8brk2SBQF03Jm3UDNTe1XqvOXHijgNWV1pybzIonkTHGGWPAeA51YeDSYVUorbApCS9Q2-RDngbs0YfeKuMe_o4h7_yYOTGkNEdS_iMgCchlWfIlXtL9uRKQTysC0vlOOQLyRaCDv0WkGkffBZUiHdUV6WBj8sF2NM6orhjoS9v6iYB82x1lJbf_vzZy93HYbE_yfD6Wn9vqnYDMgtDzYp2zcVUTXvSjsu73YPpr3LuAnwAAAP__F8mQpQ) on Democrats' push to overturn the state's six-week abortion law, though several GOP senators have expressed interest in expanding Medicaid.
## Video Shows Aftermath of Student's Fall
Newly released [police body camera video](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL3unDAQxJ_GdEasMR__wkUaukubEi14bSwZjOy9Q-TpI-4V0kw1mpnf_HnNLwwxHP437mTYu_mgq0Ripjy7kAu7TPSXtrePdB9pDwcyzapRvQSQoOczp3LSyjNU1rSNJdBjRQaGH913emh1tZled1otrXaDQ72OIyy669H-jKSV6shWwTyJAKABQIGu1dA4tazUNWiRxlbohmzglGveyFPKPqCLd_pQrte0V9FszGcR7S-hJqGm67pq5IgH4wP0JXmMQk1Pk1ATwCOtUNOS7C1X3CmjdCkxepKZPoSxSHRMeUfe5NujLPy2dHCRoyyc8i0dxijUVGVjzyvEGEo_CN34HUP87uL__fRj1L8AAAD__2bWjXg) shows the aftermath of a University of Georgia student's eight-story fall from an Athens apartment window in September. Kristin Sargent, a 21-year-old finance and marketing senior, lost her balance while dancing on furniture during a gathering at the off-campus Rambler Apartments. She fell an estimated 65 to 70 feet. Officers found her conscious and talking. Police believe poolside patio furniture, where investigators found a broken armrest, cushioned her fall. _"No one did anything bad to me,"_ Sargent told responders, confirming the fall was accidental. Her father has said he is [hopeful she will make a full recovery](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ8GOq_8t8tuQZGG7qZNiXzxMUxkbGQPa22ePiKvkGY00sz5dPT9-pq_HEVK60-3Y-Q1zAmtRjCjzIFK5VCAP9jONeKT8k7JMWYt9UMoJZSdj5LrgYVn1fvRSA9lnz1GNbzs424HY_ttNMa8vMFjGO4BdymtlvDPJ4CgrPw2PY0XUSlllVJa2ZseZNDfC-7SeYen6ayEJ87lxhtW5LKSC_GT3yi3Je99HDfmo3bmR6enTk-ttVsrvl3HTk8XvdOTfF37NZYcI1aIyqdHYlFRKJ81fgSl32eBFy4wigguXnYEaN1YVM6FUIVLwh2u8H5FGyWfm2gbRQjv0nL9L_lctk5PfRn90ShGqo-hs3LdHcV_jfl_bb9H_TcAAP__dESXsQ).

## FAA Halts Departures Nationwide
The FAA [ordered airports across the country to hold all departing flights](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ8GOp-wMfincPE3dJc2JVrsBVYx9sneg9zbR-QeIdUUnzSabz7v0x0oUFw_YEfLxzJFPEtAZszTArDm9Iy-LIHWjQufiTeIX5NqVC-kFFJP4JgOnDTU3i6gEYYarTSD7jttOl1vdugHg40e_Nz-m7Hvm6XtvMPZuN5J13Q12atPSqmllKptb_M8dKrrGqMGo7SZK92gJ075xhselFeKBEt4pQPzzaW9DnZjfpSq_V-psVLjWZAvUKnx8rkCmFIUZ8rBV2pcAASV8sQi3uQkj-JtKwqnh3DEWAR-c4aUPUXIL-Eou-deGKLDUmfrHyeFQKU3lW7WHSj8ruE_HnlY9RMAAP__sZuMXw) Friday afternoon, citing "extraordinary circumstances." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed a telecommunication outage, telling reporters, _"This isn't another 9/11."_ Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said technicians were tracking down a "communication issue," and Mullin saw no link to Thursday's global Microsoft outage. Only twice before had the FAA halted departures nationwide on this scale: on Sept. 11, 2001, and in January 2023, when a failure of the pilot-notification system grounded flights. FlightAware tracked more than 12,000 aircraft in the air worldwide Friday. The FAA [lifted the nationwide ground stop](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ8GukQe_2BcuNgmXbbdEg32GEbrQGRmifbtr7ivcMujI52j7_vznJ7IlbflN74oylmmjT5HJRFqU0Fc2v5vy0epvKxyyGeXFbe_k1Z6uAHcwE6YhE-aLPY5FrSEoacIPtjBWe9sv8YxgB3GFFRShDBkQh8CJPCpFDcG6DleewBgAUAbc5_n4LRzyuvgtfVzZxVllr3dZaWT28IbY6n_95PaPe2vvsZV5H105lenH51-4PvCuKorNOFUqdOPMsKsgrLGQMaCeQBjig5ArjgDOPYt5veHa-Vj8J1Vywu5fh_ID92cUX8FAAD__xa6dmY) at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, but delays and cancellations continued as airlines worked to restore schedules. Travelers should check with their airlines for updates.
## Most Seniors Can't Afford Assisted Living
Only 18% of older Virginians earn enough to cover assisted living where they live, [a review by the General Assembly's watchdog agency](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp_G3rAMBv8MDF2ypWtH62Iu9m0xRECI-vZVIuUJOp9Pn47O13W9AnkK-yecqEt1a8BH9lgKptUB7Cneg83O036UXB6xHBB-VtGLkXHOuFxhK1RxldBa7UAiLC1qPi1yVHJSsj20GOZhMkptfBbzZnoHs7EKURo5qtFAS_r5xzmXnHMxDJ0xixJK9ZNYJiEn08geLZWYunJgpbRTIHD-N1ZM3RbP1uujlFtuho9GXBpx-faQtu697PZYG3HxECyFnb3k3ywzyJlyQcs81Sd2sJGnQpgZBMsosCOeyDKmShtm5mJi0VtMDOzdl9xBvrVJ29uDvKc8To3s9xPIv8zKP6NWLf4CAAD__91-j8Q) found. Average monthly assisted-living costs rose 32% from 2021 to $6,940 in 2025, with regional rates ranging from $5,734 to $8,725; memory care costs about 30% more. [Del. Josh Thomas, D-Prince William](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkT2O3SAURldjdzzx-xgKF2ncTdqU1gUu9k14MALG1uw-cqSsYKqv-XSko_PrfXsHylT2n_DCZZxpK3j1jGNg2xLA3upniT1l2o_Rx1XHAeXPJrl8MiGY0BuEQSduGua4JNAIbsZFWKefRluj52PRKCwozoU3GLx5Om68RIVRvXGIIc603DwhhBZCSKUe3jsjjeFWOiu19ZPmGGnU9hgHntR2KgQpf9UT2yPU15yXY4yPPqkfk1wnuV7X9RDqVin1uh-TXKENChknuWZK9_wHsd8ZWmANT8KLJSqxM-id-sDIMp1UdhZqH51RCQ2hU9nzF_sskFJtEXxGlmpjHQvV1ie5SieYcCpZ9aaYNSYyzYNjXqJl3juOGrlJYOa2xI-Lcqb-tJPm-wso_xMa32xxLvJvAAAA__9cpZ_O), said at Monday's commission meeting that "about 80% of seniors will never be able to afford under our current system any type of assisted living." Virginia's only state subsidy for assisted living is a monthly grant for qualifying older and disabled residents, and it [pays $2,130 against a median private rate of $6,945](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFupDAQxvGnMd0iPB7jpXBxDd1ecc2VaBaPwYkXIzNhlbePNlKeIN1XfPoV__-36UYpp235Sw_2csZp4-eRWYTrFImWWj62cMScllUOeRZZaXufoIP-ovVF40SzpJMnpCb4SMg0NOy1G7C36Cw2qx-uBtCyuw7ch2CuQMYwzN3czdqwxSb5l6e1Rq01GNPe74MFazsHgwN0d4UdhySltrLymeqStkQxf5aTazuXR5P9KrIfyvxRMCoY3zLVuf15tks5FYx7iIeCsfJeqrzWv116wHYPsak-7M-Uczp6p7BbHpTytyy_jHJ6-AoAAP__yLp2YQ). About two-thirds of facilities don't serve a single grant recipient. New federal rules could let Virginia use Medicaid to help cover assisted living starting in July 2028. The watchdog also [urged lawmakers to fund more facility inspectors](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQQOGnMd0iZrDNdeHiNnSbYpuUyOAxODE_smdB-_ZRIuUJ0h99xXm_D3cXU9zmN7eS5TMMG10lETPlITg35_25-RJSnBcufO28uO1zwAb1DeAGcnATx5MG6Spvg5PkTEUWOiO1kp2S1WIJmmAMek9qGsd_0GJrdKNw1B7AB11F--0BgAQAbNt6HI1CpZoOTYeyG4VsyEfec80LnTHPcYsupNd-Uq6nfa2SXZiPItr_AnuB_Udyeap_y3reT4H94UMR2Jfnurr8Etg_DtYoHzTVhw9Vtv64Ykqx6E7IZl5dTD84__HLafErAAD__4pwd9M) and set enforceable staffing minimums.

## Broken Pump Raises Toxic Plume Concerns
A [broken pump](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAUxvGn0Q7DQUQpKLaxm223NCweBhIUAsfx3re_mXmFW3_JP_l9_x7bw8YUz-dfe6ChHPx24t0SEmHdKH9FV9J1oEdbm7f2WfN17m0TXCgGwEBupeZW0NEG_W4kjuB1jwZmLdUk9Sz7YPgywSSXRWsnR-s8ggCtPaKyQnC39NG8gwAgAUDBOCwKdyXnWdoJF_yvOslxj5TrQAFziNmn7_zCOrh89MkEotK68U8n1k6s930PNqf31onVVoouYevEWq6jMG9juioyChUt4dnYh8k-TiYAuBw550OgI_XV7OWOKcWm5k7y52Hjp9vTr896GfETAAD__55GgA8) at Chillicothe’s U.S. Paper Mill could allow a toxic underground plume to spread toward nearby homes, farmland, and the Scioto River, the company warned. The mill notified the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency that the decades-old, 90-foot pump had fractured and [needs to be replaced](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb_G3oj8MAF7YOjiLV07Ws_4EVDBICBJ-_eV8wud79XRPffrtt7QB3_cPzGSbsnZ9aBXDdQalbWlH29yeESyhKVaxHtJj2OvKx-4ZAAMxJpLqplMW6HftaAR7NyTBjULeRWzEr3T84azBC45KmsU8EnZCXAgEoqkkmPv9QkEAAEAEsbLJGmXQimBV5pok50YaPctlUtzlJxPNvymJ5WLSbEP2rWWazd-dHzp-HIa2FQMcaHOQseXraRvOlh-xMwK-kqVYcAS2Qlhb0_2FmUbHYTNMeN8CN6k5ohFHwJ7YTlqx5e-6D2_zrBK1YnhHtGH94727wOfmv8FAAD__7kdiOo), at a cost of thousands of dollars. The contamination [originated at the WearEver Aluminum factory](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yrCAUx58GO3eEZVEKitvY7W1TOkc4CDMoDJxdk7fPmDxC-t__8-O5PCGmeGz_YUdDOfjlwLMlJMK6UP6MtqTXjh6hNg-w1fw6XFvEIFTPec_lUmpuBS0tvHNG4p173aHho5bqIfUou2BW1Ah-UpMYwLqHnFYUcvVyQqfXVegumsuQcy4554rfb5NCp-Q4SnjghKtickAXKdcbBcwhZp--8hvrzea9SyYQlcbu_5iYmZjP87ywkhsBBTzaRTExQ6VoEzIxX2lMzINmYrYhphRtpoB9gYK132NKvc0HwR4PIHT97-wTCGtXjSvnJWlqZHLYdojppwb9-b-3Ed8BAAD__-Q1iOI), which operated from 1948 until the late 1990s and left trichloroethylene, lead, and cadmium in the soil and groundwater. A mill official called the failure a “potentially urgent situation” but said that residents didn’t need to worry about their water at this moment. The replacement timeline remains unclear.
## Family Dollar Settles Overcharge Claims
Ohio would [receive more than $300,000](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS3CAQRL8GZWxpEEK7AYETZefUoYqDQRoXCArmVr6_d8m_4KSTrn7d1b8-tg9Hic79p8touRxxO_HqCZmxbVz-kK_pK2NE13p0bm_l6wx9U6MyEkCC3morvaLnDYZgNU4QXwNaWF7azPq16OGwOEfvZzfFcfEY_Dx-GjUuEPH5dDEqP5C9gQCgAcDA9HgaDEYvi3YzPvHTCD1iIC7twQeWg0pM3-WN7eFLHpI9mGsX0w-hVqHW67oeF7t6m0KtN1qoFeCWSaj1zsvfhc4uIwZsLkluLqD0JWfqncopOzInzHiyvHtkQI-V6Y0yukzpW4aSkmuyNvJ07kKtQ7OhXpQSdbMIPe7ZUfq3j__72LdVfwMAAP__6KyQ_Q) under a proposed $63 million settlement over allegations that Family Dollar charged shoppers more at checkout than advertised. Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson joined the Federal Trade Commission and 16 other states in the case, alleging thousands of stores [continued overcharging](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkMGqnTAURb8mziKeJC95DjIoBQcF34XeQocS9aiBmEhyrvb-fbG_0OHebDaL9bsfeueDj-uX29FS2pYh4lUCEmEeKP3x0xFeOy7oclmcW3N6xbkMohGaA3BQw5FTOXCiAarZKpSwtBVaMK3SH6o1qtqsFpMEJ0fUExqARTbjrNE02kjVOgGVt_chACgA0CDrT42zVsYo94GfOGqmGpw9pVzThmnzaQnvdGKup7RXwW5ER2HyGxMdE911XfW9cUQpR3yvGDG7UK_pZKLrcfaOie4Lr8J_YkBXsNw5nbiPmPmNwkT32HzioPmDNsz8SY6w8B_JR979-s595EwoLXnvQ_Ap8icShSrb-bjupmjDVLPuzod_jPTfck8r_gYAAP__rcOPxg) customers despite earlier enforcement. The deal, which requires a judge’s approval, would establish a $40 million customer refund fund and a $20 million discount program. Ohio [previously sued the retailer](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZEb4B3sIHFxCNpdeiAxuD5YajOye4ebtV4x2n2Cz7irpU1X9u093nzDtj79-A0d5jdMOZ0UggjJR_p-WA58bRPClRu8fJT_3UCfZScOF4EJPR8n1gIUm0QSnQYk4NOCEHbTp9WB1s7reQqdUH4Kxeha2m2UcbK8Gb2ZhYlRNchdQCKGFEEao9mYgGG2t9j3cYDZMdxAS5dLSCnlNOeI7v6C0S94adCvRUZn6w-TI5HieZ7vPi06Xy-R4NWJyxLx45N_PAjsVj_xi_Wifu8AC6QWVH74Qz5EbtfEKRAgb7MTTzqPfEr55yIi-cPRnfSZicmyKC8eZEFM1lunusfmEn4T062lfTn4FAAD__1-ekV8) in 2022.

About 50 Ohio-grown Christmas trees will be [shipped to American troops](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLuOmDAQRb_GdEb4gYHCRRq6TZsSefEAlvxA44HN_n3k_MK2o6N759w_H9uHCzHk87dLYKlcx5bhq0YgAtyo_A37HZ8EBzish3Mnlif7uslBGi4EF3q7sdQbdtpE560GJY6lAyumRZtRL5PuLiuHRc2jmvRghFcwTsPuDzkKP2g1O_XZBdsChRBaCGGE6mcD3uhp0m6EGT4N0wP4QAV7uqBcoRzxu7yA_V5SF-1FdFemfjG5Mrm6E0PfoP4sL5PrVRIwuTYx7rLn8EKm2sAYebsyuTace7gdUoJMvGXsT6QHgVfIvvL9wlApucoJASpv9RVc5SnEQA6_ebkBHYWSWwOeCJB58-rQ-vsrxBiqmZgezuRC_P85_Xjy18p_AQAA___IC5st) in Jordan through Operation Evergreen, marking the holiday tradition’s 31st year. The trees [came from 14 Ohio farms](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMiPa47EhcHAJ2Vx6ITJ2Ay35B9lmuH37FasNNt-sSiV9qqp_r_llyFPc_pqAuqZ9nSNexWOtmOea_pM9_BlwRZPLasyW0xldmXnPJQNgIOYjp3KgrTO0Tgt8wDq2qEGNQj7FqES7azs-wQgYlmHgkmMPsu9XkFYJDtIp05K-gQAgAEDCoxskOimUEuaJAy6yET06qil3dce0U1r9R3pj7mwKrdd7rUdpHn8aPjV8uq6ri4sVdKcNn-5FDZ98ssazb2OTP8Ny_pTMZDQsYyGHsRZWMDqKGyuY32SRBQwL5sLsnqnUYAqrGfEmtFm74yLvqUjViH4LhvxXtfrrT9-afwYAAP__alqPTA) with help from veterans, students, and Scouts. The Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA) and the Ohio Christmas Tree Association will also [send homemade decorations](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd0QeINguKF5Dl9duaWEYDBIGC0iy-_cr5xe2mWZGc869X4_1YWKKef9vDlS9BL9mfLeEvWNde_mO9kzPAz2a2rwxey3P7NrKRiYpAAWxnrW0E21fYXBKIAe_DKhgWoS8i2USQ1Ajs25aQM6cL96P3m8o5Lw5DlbwZbRDVNdDABAAIIHfZolOimkS5o4zbpKIEV3spd56wBJi8emnvLDebDmGpELvZyP8H2GaMP3Rqc_jSgLXBWG6BMK0jdnGnE2PhOlrS5i-wIRpgGtwwvRWY95j3qkNNbZ-mEZtQKz04jU0jdLiDG2YXaO9IjbaC-21lLMNVbnzHVOKTU5EjPthYvo49j-X-1LsNwAA___b1ZDY) from schools, churches, and veterans’ groups, along with handwritten cards. _“Our nation’s bravest deserve the very best, and Ohio Christmas trees provide exactly that,”_ said ODA Director Brian Baldridge.

## FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop
The FAA said flights could resume Friday night after lifting a nationwide ground stop that halted every departure in the country for hours, the first since 2023 and only the second since 9/11. [Live updates here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFygzAMBuCngc05WzgmDB66sKVrR05gAeo5mDMKub59z-kjdJZO-r__6z7ckSNvyyc-yMucho1eRyQRysOS03MLh6Q98iwUMp-Ux4QygAanjFHGDjgJnzSYOviZCKipyZu2s-7q9O1Wr74dOzNeXYPgaB41hRbg5gCc1leydqrZl3PGGGtMY6270NTZrkVtTWNb1G1lNQWWlC_fiTdZaY4_6aR8mdKjjn4V2Y-q-aigr6DHvQjKqII-8kkV9H8QVSQKT0bhtKk58rLKocq6eu4BhY63qVElT5192F8cIx-uJFgeyPH9Uf7X0-nhNwAA__9MiHyD). A communications outage hit the 22 regional centers that guide planes between airports. Some 3,500 planes in the air were allowed to land, but nothing took off. Europe suspended U.S.-bound departures, Mexico grounded northbound flights, and some 11,000 flights carrying [1.5 million passengers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhTAQRE9jOhBr_G0oXKSh-2lTosVefxwZjMwGlNtHJEdIM81Ib_Tm4zk9Maa4vd5xJcshTxtdRyJmKtOr5K_NH5z3FAOTL_GkMmfkSbZS1wA1qAkdx5MmqLwNRJK6iiyYQemHbvu-Wqw2s3tg30uj_DAH541_KBmIUMu-H7CK9sYBgALolNINuUENBlsFnTLYGqFa8pFzaT5z3HihkL7zSaVxea2SXZj3Q3RvQo5Cjtd1NW6b3V0KOd5oIUeAOzohx4BY_4nVt1mz8JqqYv1-xZTioe-114ox_dL5f5-cVv4EAAD__5eOdIY) were scheduled to depart after 4 p.m. ET. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said new technology layered onto the FAA's aging analog system overwhelmed it, and that there was "no indication" of a cyberattack. Sources separately blamed a [botched software update](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O4zAMhU8jdwpMSf4rVGzjLttuadARnXChSIbMOMjtB5o5wjRsSHx83_t3Xa7IkdP9Lz7Jy5aXRO8jkgiV5V7yK4VD8h55EwqFTyprRllMa3oNoMEteBM-aYEm-I3IkG3IwzC5vuvbcWwefhwQpym0uFLX4jqZbug211sYQ7daOzTsKw4AHIB1rr_QbXLTgK0D6wZsB-VaCiy5XP5nTvKgLX7ySeVyy88m-ofIfij7R5lZmTl99nxIXSkzV7AyM0AdVpn5degqqMy8IeqEwjm9OZD-cdVVVkc-Sb_2gEL1sik-7G-OkY--Zrk_keP3b_ldY6c3XwEAAP__YQJ-7w). Microsoft said its outage was unrelated. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed "overloaded" routers, called the situation "an emergency," and asked Congress for billions more to [overhaul air traffic control](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2vnTAMQH9N2HKVryYwZOjC9rp2RIY4kDY3QcEPdP99RXuH7m_1ka1z_PNj-oCUU1l_wBM9xToVvI6MRNimtdXPEg6qe06RMLR0Ypsr0KSEslxKLs0EC6UTJ9kFHxEV6g69dIOx36zo-27zdug1WmnB2F66eYjaGmcCDCoEEWfXJX-fk1IaKbUx9oHLYAYHwkhtHAjHjMCQqLbHr5oKbRjzq57YHkt9dtlvRPvB9HemRqZGmBd3N9yQqTGnE_nnHoDwYGqMAPxfFr-7-P-YXxsQ_13qxQtQquVKAXnMad3o4NDwvYmBqVEJofu-d0yNWKi93qNBaM3U2DUf9ivlnA57669PSPmvLn3tyadXfwIAAP__UwGQ7A). ### How the Electoral College Dies Without an Amendment

Nobody is trying to repeal the Electoral College anymore. Repeal would take a constitutional amendment -- two-thirds of Congress, then 38 states. Dead on arrival, and both sides know it. Instead, the plan is simpler and entirely legal: don't change the Constitution. Change the electors.
**The mechanism**
The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (**NPVIC**) is an agreement among states. Every signatory pledges that its electors will not vote for its own statewide winner, but for the winner of the _national_ popular vote across all 50 states and D.C. The compact has a built-in trigger: it does nothing until member states collectively hold **270** electoral votes -- the number needed to win. At that moment, without one word of the Constitution changing, the presidency becomes a national popular-vote prize. Whoever wins the most votes in America wins the electors of every compact state.
**The scoreboard**
As of this month, 18 states plus the District of Columbia have enacted it -- California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont and Washington -- totaling **222 electoral votes, 82 percent of the way there. Forty-eight to go.**
Watch how they got here: Maine came aboard in 2024. Virginia -- a 13-vote state with a newly elected Democratic trifecta -- signed in April 2026. And the November midterms just delivered the movement its best map yet. As Politico reported a week after the election, the remaining path is explicit: **Pennsylvania (19), Michigan (15) and Wisconsin (10), plus either Arizona (11) or Nevada (6)** , and the compact activates -- plausibly in time to govern the 2028 election. For the first time, the people who want the Electoral College gone hold, or plausibly hold, the votes to finish it.
**The map nobody mentions**
Here's the part of the story that gets no airtime. Per the National Conference of State Legislatures, **14 states require no ID document of any kind to vote in person** -- you state your name, you sign the poll book, you get a ballot: California, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Pennsylvania and Vermont. Add D.C., and that is **198 electoral votes -- more than a third of the entire Electoral College -- cast under no-document rules.**
The five largest states on that list are California, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois and New Jersey -- 134 electoral votes between them.
Now cross-reference with the compact. Twelve of the 19 member jurisdictions -- **170 of its 222 electoral votes** -- are no-ID states. And of the 48 votes still needed to trigger it, Pennsylvania's 19 and Nevada's 6 -- 25 of the 48 -- sit in no-ID states. Pennsylvania is the crown jewel: the biggest prize on the board, the classic kingmaker, and a state where nobody is asked for identification.
**The argument**
Defenders will say: relax. Voters still sign the poll book, signatures can be audited, and prosecuted cases of illegal voting are vanishingly rare. All true. But I don't need to believe in ballot-stuffing conspiracies to see the problem, and neither should you.
The problem is asymmetry and stakes. In 2024, roughly 1.5 points separated the candidates nationally. Had the compact been active, the presidency would have turned on the aggregate national total -- every marginal vote in every state counted equally. When every vote counts equally, the integrity of every jurisdiction's checking process counts equally too. A system in which one coalition's votes run 198 electors deep in states that ask no questions, while the other's strongholds check photo ID at the door, is not one system. It is two different rulebooks wired together, and the presidency gets decided on the difference.
Elections do not need _documented_ fraud to lose legitimacy; they need the _appearance of opportunity_. Ask any losing side after any close count, in any country, what they concluded. A compact triggered on this map would put the White House within reach of whichever coalition can best maximize turnout in the jurisdictions where a signature is the only check. That is not a conspiracy theory. It is a plain description of the rules on offer for 2028.
If a national popular vote is what we want, fine -- argue for it in the open, honestly. But a national count is only as trustworthy as its weakest checkpoint. The obvious complement to a national vote count is uniform voter ID -- free, easy access, applied everywhere. The compact does the opposite: it aggregates the country's ballots without harmonizing the country's safeguards.
**What to watch**
The next move is not in Washington. It is in statehouses. Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin in the 2027 legislative sessions; Nevada as the cheap closer at six votes. Forty-eight electoral votes, four or five states, one trigger. After that, the Constitution is untouched and the Electoral College is functionally gone -- and the rules under which the next president is chosen will have been set, disproportionately, by the states that ask the fewest questions at the door.
Cobble is the right word. Watch the cobblers work.

name: Rep. Gloria Johnson
subject: Two fighters emerge: Don Leonard and Angela Gonzales-Torres are standing up!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
I want to share actions you can take from my friend Corbin Trent, because who leads our fight matters.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c269bc74d178/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7364026?e=dc5f639d62)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| | Hey Friends!
Democrats have made historic gains, but there is much work to do. Leadership matters and we need bold leadership that will put the people first. I know that many of you understand this and want something new. That is why I am sharing my friend Corbin Trent’s email—it gives you steps to make your voice heard in this upcoming decision. I am just going to post his email below....
In solidarity,Gloria

“Good morning, folks. And a good morning it is. My apologies for any typos. This is a completely dictated, unedited email. I am trying to launch an ad campaign, a massive polling series, and parent 4 kids...But! Pressure is building against leadership. In the United States Senate, we’re seeing more and more senators go on the record saying no to Chuck Schumer. It ain’t over but the efforts are working.Now, the tough nut to crack, of course, is the House of Representatives and Hakeem Jeffries. The people are speaking up. The polling is clear but representatives have a hard time listening once they’re in the swamp. Amazingly, two people: Don Leonard and Angela Gonzalez-Torres have taken the courageous step of saying no to Hakeem. As many of you know, I was the communications director for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez during her first campaign and then her first term on the Hill. One of the things that made her able to be the independent-minded representative that she was is financial support from a massive number of people. She could not be threatened with having her campaign support removed. She could not be threatened with not getting a committee assignment that gets her enough airtime that she can raise more money. She had a base of people willing to financially support her. We need to recreate that for these people that are taking a stand. I need you to donate to these people. Here, you can split your money between them. And there are some people that are going to give a lot of money, and some people that are going to give a little. It really doesn’t matter how much you put in. In D.C., money talks, period. And your money can speak volumes.[**$5, $10, Doesn’t matter, man. Click this link, put in some cash, please. It’s the most important thing that you can do to have different leadership in DC.**](https://us.list-manage.com/ySboChDqrNt?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) excitingly, we are going to be able to run the polling that I told you about yesterday. We’re also going to be able to run ads in D.C., making sure that these representatives know what’s happening outside of the bubble that they find themselves in during freshman orientation.This leadership fight in the House and in the Senate is one of the first opportunities we have to make sure that the people’s voices are not only heard but heeded. So we’re all going to have to come together and do some of the work. What can you do? Well, let me tell you what you can do. Here’s a list:[**Sign the petition started to draft Ayanna Pressley**](https://us.list-manage.com/196td_jLtpx?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) for Speaker. It doesn’t matter if you prefer her or not. What we need is somebody brave enough to step up and run. Then the emperor will be shown to be wearing no clothes. Click the image to use the tool to contact your Democratic Reps or call the switchboard at **(202) 224-3121**[****](https://us.list-manage.com/Q6EAQbTqSf6?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)

Right now, the voters are being loud. We’re speaking up. We’re signing petitions, calling Representatives and Senators, and applying pressure. If we keep this up, what we can show is that democracy still matters in the Democratic Party, that voters still matter, that our opinions matter. Win, lose, or draw, these fights are important because they’re allowing us to build the muscle memory and the systems to have these battles. This is going to be the first of many. So if you want change, if you want Medicare for all, if you want a health care system that provides services for people at a reasonable price and rapid speed, if you want an economy where people can afford housing and health care, childcare, where we’re not subject to the whims of a few, but the needs of the many are what drives our policy, then we’re going to go through fights just like this over and over until the people have more power. But again, the most important thing we can do is empower the people that stand up and give them a safety net that allows them to take a stand for us the against the powerful people in the party. [So please click this link and donate to Angela Gonzales - Torres and Don Leonard. ](https://us.list-manage.com/yCtpO1atT1H?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)Thank you for being here,Corbin Trent

Madison Brooks, a 19-year-old LSU sophomore, died on January 15, 2023, after being struck by a car on Airline Highway in the pre-dawn hours. Prosecutors say she was raped earlier that night by more than one of four men who had left a Baton Rouge bar with her; the men say any sexual contact was consensual. Four were arrested; three remain charged -- Desmond Carter, Casen Carver, and Kaivon Washington. None has been tried; all are presumed innocent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fed0ce12-cf6d-4d88-9357-70c1637b2e65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The judge and her son**
The cases landed with Judge Gail Horne Ray of the 19th Judicial District Court -- and that's where the story gets its twist. Court records and local reporting (The Advocate, WBRZ, WAFB) establish that her son, Nelson Dan Taylor Jr., pleaded guilty in the late 1990s to multiple rapes -- counts of forcible and aggravated rape, plus aggravated burglaries -- with victims who were teenage girls, reportedly including classmates from his Baton Rouge high school. Ray, then a practicing lawyer, was his defense attorney.
Taylor, now 46, went back to court this year seeking to have those convictions set aside. Last year he pleaded guilty to an obscenity charge from a 2024 hotel incident -- allegedly exposing himself to a hotel worker -- while he was already on probation. Because judges customarily recuse themselves from matters involving a colleague's family, his filings end up in front of the one judge in the building who can't recuse: his mother.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/620c8790-fcec-41d3-8138-fabacd5ffc3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The recusal war**
Once the son's history surfaced, District Attorney Hillar Moore moved to remove Ray from Carver's trial. The motion leaned on text messages Carver sent his father -- including "her son was accused of rape a while back so she knows to help us," and claims they were "friends with the judge." On November 3, 2025, Judge Brad Myers granted the recusal, and the First Circuit affirmed.
Then the Louisiana Supreme Court reversed it. In May 2026 it ruled that prosecutors had failed to prove why Ray should be removed, and it later denied a rehearing bid -- reinstating her. When the story went national in August (Fox News, New York Post), the DA pressed again to remove her from the cases against all three defendants; the state's highest court has left her in place. So the post's core claim -- lower courts ordered her off, the Supreme Court kept her on -- is accurate, just condensed.
Critics also point to a pattern: local outlets report the DA separately asked the Supreme Court to void Ray's ruling that threw out another man's rape conviction -- after that defendant had asked her to reduce his sentence so he could seek parole.
**The pink-clothing sideshow**
Over the summer, a defense attorney filed a motion asking to bar spectators from wearing pink -- Brooks' family and friends wear it in her memory -- arguing it was courtroom advocacy. Ray ruled in August that pink was allowed, though not shirts bearing Brooks' image. This month she found attorney Caitlin Fowlkes in contempt for using Brooks' full name in that motion, then declined to impose any penalty beyond an admonition.
**What it actually tests**
Louisiana law requires a judge to step aside when partiality is proven or when her impartiality "might reasonably be questioned" -- but the burden sits on whoever moves for recusal, and the Supreme Court found the state hadn't met it. The irony is symmetrical: the defendant's own texts said the judge "knows to help us," while prosecutors argued that a judge who once defended her son against serial rape charges shouldn't now be deciding rape charges. Neither proves actual bias; both are reasons a reasonable observer might doubt neutrality. That gap -- between what can be legally proven and what the public can unsee -- is the entire story.
One caveat: the post's race-first framing (Black judge, white victim) is not what any filing argues. The legal fight has been entirely about family history, appearance of fairness, and who bears the burden of proving doubt.
**Where it stands**
Carver faces a bench trial in late November; Carter a jury trial on December 7 -- both before Ray, with Washington's case still pending. For the Brooks family, every ruling in the coming weeks will come from the one judge in the courthouse whose own family file contains the crime their daughter's case is about. Louisiana's highest court has decided that's legally survivable. Whether it looks like justice -- to them, or to anyone watching -- is the question her courtroom will answer by Christmas.

Marco Polo, the nonprofit research group that spent years on the Biden laptop, announced its next project Tuesday: the federal judiciary.
Founder Garrett Ziegler says the group decided "a new multi-year beat is needed." He calls federal judges "a new caste system in the United States."
[| | | | | Marco Polo
---
@MarcoPolo501c3
Watch & hear abt what we're doing next. Federal judges are an elite caste in America, and the public is in the dark abt many of their machinations. In other words, they're a worthy topic of our inquiry. This new beat should be fun and, more importantly, extremely revelatory.
| 5:51 PM * Nov 10, 20261.59K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/2329cc68-997f-494e-8d6b-0fe6de736246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The project is a website, [ThirdBranch.icu](https://substack.com/redirect/29240dbe-7f6e-4f92-887c-d781412cedc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Its own description: a directory of the Senate-confirmed federal judiciary that "details every judge's professional & family connections & any potential conflicts that could/should warrant recusal."
In the video, Ziegler promises financial disclosures, "who they're married to, what their adult children are doing." He says there will be more than 1,400 profiles "in the next year plus," and that "there's going to be no subscription sold." He also asks for tips from anyone with experience before these judges. He says the profiles aren't all built yet.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Z9n7LQvAB-YgzgZ3N1TsUAsWhvcohCENEwbFs4ccaOE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224391431)
His case against the bench: lifetime jobs, big pay, and "senior status" that he says keeps the pay.
The federal courts' [salary table](https://substack.com/redirect/77bda9f4-3a56-4b25-9d5d-b6f4b2dc96cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has district judges at $249,900 and circuit judges at $264,900 for 2026 (salary). He also says only eight judges since 1789 have been impeached and removed, making a federal judgeship one of the most lucrative tenured jobs in America. The [Federal Judicial Center's list](https://substack.com/redirect/44b3f3f1-930c-4397-a540-4e20180fc98e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has eight.
Maine's federal bench is small, and the public record on it is already thick. However, the judicial transparency website is fairly thin on new disclosures.
**The district court:** Chief Judge [Lance Walker](https://substack.com/redirect/af1983f1-e062-4958-b05a-5919ed5cfaa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was nominated by Donald Trump and confirmed in October 2018. He became chief in 2024. [Stacey Neumann](https://substack.com/redirect/d9648628-1bd8-49b4-8144-182db328024e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was nominated by Joe Biden and confirmed in July 2024. Before that she was an assistant U.S. attorney and sat on Maine's ethics and election commission. Judge John Woodcock has been on the court since 2003. Nancy Torresen took senior status on October 11, 2025. As of November 10, her seat is [still vacant](https://substack.com/redirect/dbf384e7-c9e3-4c82-b82c-6f0ebf4330bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with no nominee listed.
**The appeals court:** Joshua Dunlap, a Portland private-practice lawyer until then, was [nominated by Trump and confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/b2e992b8-7d99-4035-9efb-4a81c92fca71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the First Circuit on November 4, 2025, by a [52-46 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/6f711432-45a4-4197-bc25-4a08cac373f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**What they've ruled.**
Voter data: On May 21, 2026, Walker [dismissed the Justice Department's suit](https://substack.com/redirect/50dc05ba-05e1-41f5-af32-47f6b8adbaa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demanding Maine's unredacted voter list, writing that "states are the primary regulators and administrators of elections for federal office, unless Congress passes legislation that preempts that framework." In other words, a Trump appointee blocked the Trump Administration's effort to purge non-citizens from Maine's voter rolls.
School funding: On April 11, 2025, Woodcock [ordered USDA to release](https://substack.com/redirect/e48004b1-b6ea-47b7-b29d-d3e4ea5c1b31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) funds it froze over Maine's transgender athlete policy. The order said it wasn't weighing in on that dispute, only on whether USDA followed required procedure.
ICE: In [January 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/03546edf-4374-4d54-8c8d-2bc8ce48cf7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Woodcock ordered two men returned to Maine after ICE moved them against a court order. In [June](https://substack.com/redirect/b5474a13-9e1b-4b92-a282-33dfa579714f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Neumann ordered a Lewiston man released after the same thing.
Sentencing: The Maine Wire reported Neumann gave [Ken Yiu time served](https://substack.com/redirect/6aaf6650-b195-4bf7-acc8-580d8758bf2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a mortgage fraud and grow-house case. Neumann, like Maine's state judges, has been bizarrely lenient with the few members of Chinese cannabis cartels who end up in court.

Four firefighters killed in the Knowles Fire had nine seconds between learning their helicopter couldn't land and deploying emergency shelters, according to a [federal investigation](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yhCAUhZ8GOxzAK0pBkcZu06Z0EC7K7N3FQWadvH3GZN8g7bk_c77v6zbfXKL0XD_dA231cX7ieRDWimW-P_NJeMRUsOCeS90zpWMtblZCaS4llzDvJR87-jrLJtgYlXe6QSsHA1pL6Ptms9EHbVwA2UcAr40xCMMCy4KdHyGKJtnroZQSZCdA9q3r4jgI0SuDWnfQMRAYUs2lrRv6TLm4kCN95xeW1udHQ3ardT9Y98HUxNR0nmdrLpRrytTkSk2ekKnpCpmaKHtH12KicAEyNUUMWBzxP1Z-pTGtW8Vy8HsiwsDfRvj7Yug4SqWWqAbeC6849Avy0cuRC5BmiIsAoX1TbNjPRJQOPTAQ68Ml-q1d_6v8ZdVPAAAA__8NQJYv) released Thursday. The Rifle Helitack crew was working two tiny fires in Mesa County on June 27 when the larger Snyder Fire, which ran more than 7 miles in under three hours, overtook them. Emily Barker, Nick Hutcherson, and Sydney Watson died at the scene, and Nathan Matthews died July 24. The Interior Department's serious accident investigation assigns no blame. It cites extreme fire behavior, strained communications, [understaffing, and gaps in aerial supervision](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd46YAYNTULzGXV67pUVgsFGIsYBNlL9fObv7BduMRprRPTr34zJfbExxW_7bO5nmwrzRsyZqjcp82_IzUQ2xUKE9l7bnFOtS7IwcVQ_Qg5z3kutOrs3QeRMCOqs6MqDPUimQw9CtBjTXgx2EdiidvfIwaj8GKbXUOF6t6KI5AgFAguAShpMVYdScD3gmpYQUTHLyseVyaiu5nHKxPof0yg8qJ5fvXTJra3tl4h_DieH0-1M_t-POcDoIDCeAYyDD6ceur9vLU-kPy_5b872HuKyNSu1vMSXyDKeuGL8_Y0qxKs0kX-42pje9_bW5h8GvAAAA__8M94OT). The lone survivor held a shelter down against the wind for 48 minutes. About two and a half hours after the burnover, a pilot spotted a strobe light through the smoke. The report lists [19 findings](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0SAMV4XFNu4y7ZbWqwZ7FEIY8HIUf5-5bz3B68-0tU95-99uQfMWLY_4Qme17QUeLUMzFCXR6FXhpawQoWDKh-UsW01LEYZJ7WW2i5HpXbAyovuok_JrMF14PU4Wee0HYZu9xPYEZSOEaCP05BGCC7GMYaUYPjnpg79Nai1trpXVg-30Kdfo1KDmcC53vbCKojIVG-8w0qZaoiU8ptOqLeVnl32O_PRRP9bmFmY-RHPDxBmvoSEmTOtIQszYzmhMW6BkYr88mqyQKj5LY2SCUvEsjWJhUle7gm3naE2GSHwfgH5XeaDhZm76uPxwpyxuVFYtT0D5s8v_mnT05v_AQAA__9U0pDq) and no recommendations. _"In wildland fire, we honor those we have lost by learning,"_ it concludes.

## FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop
The Federal Aviation Administration [ordered a nationwide ground stop](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OrDAMBeCnCV1G-SMZihS3oZvbboksYsBShiDwMNp5-lXYR9jaln2-8_UYHkCZ1vk_PDEyfKZhxfeRkRn3YQJYgamsb0o47-W1poPLtpTBKOOl1lK7AUamEwcHTYrWj11wDUYdOue9bm1olmhABURnk7OoAoDybTJmSl3y-t55aCjWe1prp61qrbul1qK-Bz_6gL41RjiFibjsN14QdvqUFab8XU7cb2N5NjkuzNsh7D9hemF62KqijoTpM50oTP-bX1aAhJMul5wyzQsfsq7L15aA8bhcVtZIzR7T9qac6fBBODU_gfL1kf9a1hnNTwAAAP__voB_GA) Friday, halting departures at all U.S. airports after communications problems affected multiple air route traffic control centers. Flights already in the air were allowed to continue to their destinations. The [FAA said every flight was accounted for](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO5CAYBODT4AyLl2EdEGzirDfd0PrNo_1LNLQAtzV9-pFngjnAxCVV6av_t_UGmDDf_8Ej2A7vuOZwthR6D3WNABk6lnyiD_dajuxbL8-9rIIJTTmnXK3gOr7CqmDwVmo3GzUEy82stOaTNMNutWF-25jnwhitIouRKcZnKZ1Q8yb0gPbq45wrLtkk1egnGfgfo502QU9CEMWCx17q2PcAFd8lQ0wf5RXq6MpjSHbv_dmI_EvEQsRynucIm-PTlRKxHI1eLCKWCECxtSM0-kOj3zZ64WjJ9GgUsNJeIUZ0Q7X-eWJK2LQhit0fgOlrtv_2sZcVnwEAAP__9VyBew), with international arrivals handled case by case. The stop began shortly before 4 p.m. EST and was lifted shortly after 8 p.m. The FAA [told Fox News](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LuOqzAQBuCngc7IN-xQuDgNXU67JZo14zCSsSPswG6efkVS7ANsOZqL5vs_rtMVKFK6_YcVXYVnmBIeJWKtuE0BIEGlnA6a8bblR5pLzfclT5JLw4RgQk_gK-04aWhnp4wfrG7RCTtoY0SvbLu4YPkQes4NQu_hU_AguboI00tl1MUPLbnznhBCC8V7pbu5Vygu1nhj0fRSNprjTDVvXV0QNnrmBCF-5x23zue1jW6p9V4a9a-RYyPH4zi6kL9Oytlv5BhpR3bWjRwDAKNSHljYL4-9fewEMk8VC_N5XR-J_GumvFfazc33g2KkYmyj-W0Fiq8f6l_j2538CQAA__-bC4fi) the outage was not a cyberattack, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said it posed no threat to public safety. In Arizona, departures were [grounded at Phoenix Sky Harbor, Mesa Gateway, Scottsdale, and other airports](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQhU9jMiP8TwcONiHrTTdEhV1uLBmMbG-j7tOPmBlpDjBJRaXvvff9u893iCnuj7-woW3wDvOOZ03YGpY5AOzQYt7P6PFR8v_d15aPNc984JoyRpmcwbX4xFlC563Q7mZkh5aZm9SaKWG61epbwBAEAzWoUQzGCTW6xY2D8wKXsHTRXjzGmGRiUEL2Xglko9FOG9SKcyIH9LHl0rcVocR33iGkV35i6V3eumTX1o5KxB_CJ8Kn8zx7eAfYYnpdD4RPVwLhE2PXEYRPEMuRS6sUXMm10m8shRDQNfR0edGf9TQA0C8F9HJA-NQV648zphSrNkQOjw1i-qzTfmvyaflHAAAA__-6m4mS). This is just the second time since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that the FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop. The only other case since was January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned.
## Mayes Seeks Execution for Trooper's Killer
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes asked the state Supreme Court to [set a Jan. 27 execution date](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unDAUhVdjOiOuf0PhIg3dS5sS3dgXcJ6xkfEMmVl9RJQdvOZUR9_5-fkxf2BMMa8_cCfX8L3Mma4zUWtU5wUxY4slXzHQWssjh7OVYyuzGIThABzUjL7FJ80Ku-Ck8aNVHTmwozIGtLTd5oxexC8L3grtQY1BG5TSkxLjaBcaoIvu5gGAAjloqfqgJcE3a7yxZLQQTA0UYiu1bxthje-ScUmv8qTa-7J3yW2tHSeT35mYmJiu6-rxveAe0-s2MDHdCUxMALdIJqb_GI4rx_Pz5L8xc2E5_SH_uDfzgI34jplfW-GfMSUKvNVSDqocxlEzMXXVheOKKcXTWKaGdceY_jVqXz3z6cTfAAAA__9nE4fj) for the man who killed a state trooper on the Beeline Highway in 1995. Ernesto Martinez shot and killed Trooper Bob Martin, 57, [a 27-year DPS veteran](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OhCAYxJ8GO4z8EbSguMZur73SfMKnkrBgkJXsPv1lN_cG181kkpnJ7-c238AHH7dvuKMp8FrniPUMWArmeQWIUHyK1TvccnpEd5Z07GnmHVeUMcrkDLb4C2cJjTNC2VHLBg3To1SK9UI3uwFrHcNFs5EPWiirFivGQTDbiUWoZW28efcxxiQTXS9k63qBbNDKKo2q55zIDp0vKbdlR8j-lSKs4ZkuzK1N9yaYvZTjJOKL8InwqdbaOjwxY3nnhE9sHHvCp-Et1cezQY-CEz5dWDBDpGldvcVMt0eM6KhLNdIU6d8c3f22V3jSHekBJacQ0BE-Ndm4o_oQ_Kk0kd12Bx8-p8p_eV6G_wYAAP__ayWJmg), during a traffic stop north of Shea Boulevard on Aug. 15, 1995. During two days on the run, Martinez killed a second person in California before he was captured. He was convicted in 1997 and sentenced to death the next year, and prosecutors say he has [exhausted his state and federal appeals](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOiP8gwmFi23osu2WaGIPwRLY7DDE2Tz9iqv7Brf_dPSd8-c-3SGuMT1_w4aO4TNPCcuxIjPSNAMk4JhTiQGflM8UDs77kifVKiukFNJM4Dm-cDJQB6etH3pTo5P9YKyVne7rxWFneuOHR7Cgzc0af1MPb7RXqmuD0lBHd_GklEbqttOmCZ1Geeuttz3aTqnKtBgiZ2p4QaD4yQnm9V9-ITU-b_XqFub9qPSvSo2VGkspzZzfst2XjCm-r1GlxkutUuM3QBD-PfHgQ-Ab_Xl5igJEkFggJTw4iw2IY8KPkMPQCaacdySxnRSQanJhL3Fd42H7yrTPDeL6dYd_WvLl1P8AAAD__8X8i9s). They argue that a 2019 court challenge he filed, which is still pending, doesn’t stand in the way. Martinez’s lawyer has [accused Mayes of rushing the execution](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFywjAMgOGncTY4W5aVZPDQJRtdO-ZErBDfmZhLBLQ8fY--Qtd_-Ib_6zSeOJe8Xj75KlH5NY-rPPciqrKNM_PKmuv6zEkuW72vadd6W-oIFujg3MHhyJPmh4zITYqepr7FRqJreyRywbfNEs_dOc0EPkCHYD0gJnuWuUPyFIKjJse355xD523weEzBi-tamqgVCgAGraSsdTvqIrzlV115Lj_1IdtxqtemxEX1thv_YWAwMHy_q4GBX5OsunExMOzKet8NDGD7YC2hdb0ndNCha7aYbs9cSt6pNWgvV87lT9b_TnlE-A0AAP__S1tzHw) ahead of her reelection race. Arizona has 108 people on death row.
## Tucson Welcomes Home Honor Flight Veterans
Dozens of people [turned out at Tucson International Airport Thursday night](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OtCAYha8GO4z8CGNB8TV287VbGoQXJcuAwVfNztVvnFvY5hTnJE9Onq_n9LQxxbz8ty8waN9hynDtCRChTsHabDGWfEUPSy1H9juWbS0T77iijFEmJ-swnjBJ23gjlBu0bMAwPUilWC90s5qHdJ0GJ-Ywe5jDQ_FBzr5jUoZBD3puorl5jDHJRNcL2fpeAHto5ZQG1XNOZAc-YqktrmBrfJdsQ_opJ9TWlVeTzIq47UT8I3wkfLyuq_0uyd8j4eNNJ3xk7A7xKegJCNXmnVbAo2aKh9tLpjYgVLqWXCoNKS4rUqxxo94RPjbV-O2KKcVdaSK75WVj-hzAv7o7Df8NAAD__5nyg08) to cheer 20 Southern Arizona veterans home from a free Honor Flight trip to Washington, D.C. The group, made up of three Korean War veterans and 17 Vietnam veterans, [left Tuesday on Honor Flight Southern Arizona's 37th trip](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OnDAUBeCnMd1F-Ad7KCjS0G3alOhiXw_WGntk7oKyTx9NlDdIfaRP55xfH-sHppzK8yceNDN-x7XQfWZiprZGxIKcarlToGerXyWcXF97XdWgLEgJ0qzoOV20GuzCrK2fnOlolm4y1spRu26fBxxHL3V00W5bUG4iT3ajaMfH5Em7Ls1vT0pppB5GbfowapIPZ711ZEelhBkoJK6t552wpe9aMObf9aLW-3p0ed6ZX6fQP4RahFru--4_r4rvUKjlPUmoJVePWahFDXDWL96pFfiHwUVMDcsJjJ8ENUaoBfZaaoOY03Nn4AoBvFALNk4-06rtNJloDGyb9mAmNPCIzsK2xUFtQY0eVb_zkbs2h9edck6ndcIMzwNT_tub__fya1Z_AgAA__-qepZ3). They spent Veterans Day visiting the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Wall and the World War II, Korean War, and Lincoln memorials. When Vietnam veteran Bob Taylor came home decades ago, he and other service members [were chased through the Denver airport terminal](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OnDAUBeCnMZ0R_sEeChdp6DZtSnTX9zJYMTYyd0DZp48myhtsfaRP55xfH8sHpJzK8yfsFBi-1qXQfWZiprasAAU41XInpGerr4In12Orix60k0pJZReInC5aLHQYjIuTtx0F5SfrnBqN77YwqRWnhwO_Ooz-U5sY4wpjtGQ8OW-6FN6eUsoqM4zG9jgaUg_vovPkRq2FHQgT19bzRtDSVy2w5j_1otbHunc5bMzHKcwPoWeh5_u--99XhXco9PyeJPSca4Qs9HzWF2_UivwvyYv4lDflWHdCudWdJLDkVzxrkZDaURsLPUPjFDMtn_ahh2lEOaJGaa1FCQggo3cO3WOYImC_8Z67FvC4U87pdF7Y4blDyv8K83e_voL-GwAA__9gmJVK). _"This kind of takes the place of that, the welcome home we missed, so we really appreciate it, "_ Taylor said Thursday.
